analysis: Examined the two base_text excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 5075-6861) together with the patch excerpt. The visible changes are only prompt_contract_id and chain_hash value substitutions, for example 6bb9fb05... to 8171fec3... at lines 7, 72, 239, 5999 and 6537, plus block-boundary chain_hash lines such as 6004, 6718 and 6722. The file is a public golden-vector fixture of synthetic data ("Public followup", "Public synthetic cache-parity input"). It contains no secrets, keys, tokens or consumer content. No code, authorization, attestation, encryption or coordinator/provider protocol logic changes in the supplied evidence. Security relevance is limited to the prompt-contract ID and chain-hash derivation used by the prefix cache (T-041, TB-007). Changing the contract ID invalidates existing cache artifacts keyed to the old ID, which is a safe fail direction if the Go and Swift implementations agree. The supplied evidence does not show the implementation that computes the new ID, whether the Swift and Go sides are updated in lockstep, or whether the change alters cache isolation or scope binding. Token IDs and request bodies appear unchanged in the visible hunks, but the range map is incomplete and the patch is truncated, so the later parts of the file are not verified. I did not observe a regression. The remaining integration questions are whether the generator and consumers agree on the new contract ID, and whether the contract change reflects a semantic change to template or tokenization that other units must review.
